Marathon Petroleum rose 1.46% today as oil refining fundamentals tightened further. U.S. refineries are running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum utilization—while storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain modest. This combination supports refiner margins because tight capacity means refineries can't easily increase output if demand holds, and lower inventories leave less cushion against supply disruptions.

The broader backdrop is sustained geopolitical tension: the U.S. Navy blockade is slashing Iran's oil exports as part of an economic pressure campaign, and six months into the conflict, markets are treating it as an indefinite stalemate rather than an imminent resolution. That persistence in regional risk, combined with tight U.S. refining capacity, is supporting the refiner sector even though crude prices remain modest by recent standards.
